meta.title: Muscle Tissue
meta.summary: Tissue specialized for contraction — one of the four basic tissue types, responsible for producing movement.

blocks.name: Muscle tissue
blocks.def: Tissue specialized for contraction — one of the four basic tissue types, responsible for producing movement.

blocks.name: Contractility
blocks.def: Long muscle cells shorten and generate a pulling force.

blocks.name: Excitability
blocks.def: An electrical nerve impulse stimulates the muscle cell to contract.

blocks.name: Extensibility
blocks.def: Muscle can be stretched back to its original length by contraction of an opposing muscle.

blocks.name: Elasticity
blocks.def: Muscle can recoil after being stretched.

blocks.name: Functions of muscle tissue
blocks.def: Producing motion; stabilizing body positions; storing and moving substances within the body; generating heat (thermogenesis).

blocks.x: Structurally, muscles are classified according to the appearance of their contractile cells (which contain thin actin filaments and thick myosin filaments):

blocks.name: <term d="Showing a banded, striped appearance under the microscope.">Striated</term> muscle
blocks.def: Cells exhibit visible cross-striations under the light microscope — includes skeletal and cardiac muscle.

blocks.name: Smooth muscle
blocks.def: Cells do not exhibit cross-striations.

blocks.name: Voluntary muscle
blocks.def: Skeletal muscle — under conscious control.

blocks.name: Involuntary muscle
blocks.def: Cardiac and smooth muscle — some have the intrinsic ability to initiate their own contraction; contraction is otherwise stimulated by autonomic nerve impulses, hormones, and local metabolites.

blocks.name: Skeletal muscle (overview)
blocks.def: Attaches to bone, skin, or fascia; striated with light and dark bands visible under the microscope; under voluntary control of contraction and relaxation.

blocks.name: Skeletal muscle fiber structure
blocks.def: Long, cylindrical, non-branching fibers. Multinucleated, with peripheral (edge-located) nuclei. Show striation.

blocks.name: Skeletal muscle regeneration
blocks.def: Skeletal muscle fibers cannot divide and have limited powers of regeneration. Satellite cells, located between the plasma membrane of a mature muscle fiber and its external lamina, enable repair of damaged fibers.

blocks.name: Origin of multinucleation
blocks.def: Skeletal muscle fibers form by the fusion of many myoblasts during development, which is why they end up multinucleated.

blocks.x: <term d="The tissue that supports, binds and separates other tissues, rich in matrix between its cells.">Connective Tissue</term> Sheaths in Skeletal Muscle

blocks.name: Epimysium
blocks.def: Dense regular connective tissue that surrounds the entire muscle. The major vascular and nerve supply of the muscle penetrates the epimysium.

blocks.name: Perimysium
blocks.def: Connective tissue that surrounds a group of muscle cells, bundling them into a fascicle.

blocks.name: Endomysium
blocks.def: A thin layer of connective tissue that surrounds each individual muscle cell.

blocks.name: Aponeurosis
blocks.def: A flat, sheet-like <term d="A strong cord of fibrous tissue that attaches muscle to bone.">tendon</term>.

blocks.name: Fascia
blocks.def: A dense irregular connective tissue that lines the body wall and limbs, holding functional muscle units together.

blocks.name: Skeletal muscle functions & location
blocks.def: Contraction is usually under voluntary/conscious control — involved in facial expression, movement, maintaining posture, stabilizing joints, and generating body heat. Found attached to bones (occasionally to skin, e.g. facial muscles), and also in the tongue, pharynx, and upper esophagus.

blocks.name: Cardiac muscle (overview)
blocks.def: Striated in appearance; involuntary control; autorhythmic because of a built-in pacemaker.

blocks.name: Cardiac muscle fiber structure
blocks.def: Broader, shorter, branching fibers. Generally uninucleated (single central nucleus), though some cells are binucleated.

blocks.name: Intercalated discs
blocks.def: Specialized junctions where cardiac muscle cells interdigitate with one another, containing gap junctions that let electrical signals pass between cells.

blocks.name: Cardiac muscle regeneration
blocks.def: No regenerative activity under normal conditions.

blocks.name: Cardiac muscle autorhythmicity
blocks.def: Cardiac muscle cells are able to generate their own action potentials; they do not require nerve impulses to contract.

blocks.name: Anatomy of cardiac muscle (summary)
blocks.def: Striated, short, quadrangular-shaped, branching fibers, each with a single centrally located nucleus, connected by intercalated discs with gap junctions; has the same arrangement of thick and thin filaments as skeletal muscle.

blocks.name: Smooth muscle (overview)
blocks.def: Attached to hair follicles in the skin, and found in the walls of hollow organs (blood vessels, GI tract); nonstriated in appearance; involuntary.

blocks.name: Smooth muscle fiber structure
blocks.def: Narrow, spindle-shaped cells, usually lying parallel to one another; a single central nucleus; no striations.

blocks.name: Smooth muscle functions
blocks.def: Specialized for slow, prolonged contraction; propels substances along internal passageways. Capable of dividing to maintain or increase cell number (unlike skeletal or cardiac muscle).

blocks.name: Smooth muscle location
blocks.def: Mostly the walls of hollow organs (gut, genitourinary/renal system, blood vessels), and the intrinsic muscles of the eye.

blocks.name: Muscle fiber
blocks.def: A muscle cell — long, cylindrical, and multinucleated.

blocks.name: Sarcolemma
blocks.def: The muscle cell membrane.

blocks.name: Sarcoplasm
blocks.def: The cytoplasm of a muscle cell; filled with tiny threads called myofibrils and myoglobin (a red-colored, oxygen-binding protein).

blocks.name: Transverse (T) tubules
blocks.def: Invaginations of the sarcolemma into the center of the cell, filled with extracellular fluid; carry muscle action potentials down into the cell.

blocks.name: Terminal cisternae
blocks.def: Regions of the sarcoplasmic reticulum that store calcium.

blocks.name: Myofibrils
blocks.def: Threads filling the muscle fiber, separated by sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR).

blocks.name: Myofilaments
blocks.def: The thick and thin contractile protein filaments within a myofibril.

blocks.name: Sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR)
blocks.def: A system of tubular sacs similar to smooth ER in non-muscle cells; stores Ca²⁺ in a relaxed muscle; release of Ca²⁺ triggers muscle contraction.

blocks.name: Sarcomere
blocks.def: The basic contractile compartment of a muscle fiber, separated by Z discs. Thick and thin filaments overlap in a pattern that creates striations (light I bands and dark A bands); in the overlap region, six thin filaments surround each thick filament.

blocks.name: Relative resistance of muscle to disease
blocks.def: Muscle tissues experience relatively few disorders — heart muscle is the main exception. Skeletal muscle is remarkably resistant to infection; smooth muscle problems mostly stem from external irritants.

blocks.name: Muscular dystrophy
blocks.def: A group of inherited, muscle-destroying diseases. Affected muscles enlarge with fat and connective tissue while the muscle itself degenerates.

blocks.name: Duchenne muscular dystrophy
blocks.def: A sex-linked recessive form of muscular dystrophy.

blocks.name: Myotonic dystrophy
blocks.def: A form of muscular dystrophy causing skeletal-muscle spasms followed by muscle weakness and abnormal heart rhythm.

blocks.name: Fibromyositis (fibromyalgia)
blocks.def: A group of conditions involving chronic inflammation of a muscle, its connective tissue coverings, tendons, and the capsules of nearby joints. Symptoms are nonspecific: fatigue, frequent awakening from sleep, severe musculoskeletal pain, and headache. Affects mostly women.

blocks.name: Muscle tissue with age
blocks.def: The amount of connective tissue in muscle increases while the number of muscle fibers decreases, leading to loss of muscle mass — muscular strength can decrease by about 50% by age 80.

blocks.name: Sarcopenia
blocks.def: Age-related muscle wasting.

blocks.name: Myalgia
blocks.def: Muscle pain.

blocks.name: Myopathy
blocks.def: Any disease of muscle tissue.

blocks.name: Hypertrophy
blocks.def: An increase in the size of a tissue or organ due to enlargement of its individual cells.

blocks.name: Hyperplasia
blocks.def: An increase in the size of a tissue or organ due to an increase in the number of its cells.

blocks.name: Dysplasia
blocks.def: Abnormal development or growth of cells, tissue, or organs.

blocks.name: Actin
blocks.def: The protein making up the thin filaments in a muscle cell's sarcomere.

blocks.name: Myosin
blocks.def: The protein making up the thick filaments in a muscle cell's sarcomere.

blocks.name: Z disc
blocks.def: The structure marking the boundary between adjacent sarcomeres, anchoring the thin filaments.

blocks.name: A band
blocks.def: The dark band of a sarcomere, corresponding to the full length of the thick (myosin) filaments.

blocks.name: I band
blocks.def: The light band of a sarcomere, containing only thin (actin) filaments.

blocks.name: Myoblasts
blocks.def: Embryonic precursor cells that fuse together to form a mature, multinucleated skeletal muscle fiber.

blocks.name: Satellite cells
blocks.def: Stem cells located between the plasma membrane of a mature skeletal muscle fiber and its external lamina, responsible for repairing damaged muscle fibers.

blocks.name: Thermogenesis
blocks.def: Heat generation — one of the key functions of muscle tissue, especially involuntary shivering of skeletal muscle.

blocks.name: Autorhythmicity
blocks.def: The intrinsic ability of a tissue (like cardiac muscle) to generate its own rhythmic contractions without external nerve stimulation.
